body:
Accepted full negative answer to Novak's universal expected p-th-power discrepancy comparison (joint work with Hinrichs; OWR 13/2004, printed p. 698; problem 30000052 / OWR-723-005). All original continuous-generator/independent-shift, normalized anchored-box and even-exponent conventions are retained.

Published preprint: **[10.5281/zenodo.23442649](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23442649)**. [Zenodo record and downloads](https://zenodo.org/records/23442649) include the four-page research note and exact source/verification archive. Author: Alec Kriebel, ORCID 0009-0001-9320-500X; version 1.0.0, 17 October 2026; CC BY 4.0.

The exact n=3, d=1, p=4 lattice fourth moment is 19/1620 > iid 4/405, with gap 1/540 and ratio 19/16. Three is the smallest possible counterexample point count: complete ensemble laws agree at n≤2 in every dimension. The independent empty-tail proof gives2/[105(n-1)] > iid(3n-1)/(30n^3) for every integer n≥4 in dimension one. Expected second moments equal (2^(-d)-3^(-d))/n for all n,d. A separate exact affine-cell calculation reproduces the supplementary n=4 value 139/17280. No inference about expected norms or failure of good-generator existence is made.

Parent and three distinct independent mathematical families reconstructed the proof and exact primary target. Seven pinned standard-library verification programs pass ordinary and optimized modes, comparing complete mathematical outputs and exercising explicit failure guards where supplied. The source archive preserves all ten original PR files unchanged, standalone proofs, full new audits and source/chronology records. Computation supplements the analytic proof; no formal proof-assistant certification is claimed.

Two successive fresh independent whole-package adversarial reviews passed the identical release without unresolved issues: [review1](https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/blob/f2c69a9d6fc1194aa61bc59459c527eb84615168/draft_pr_actual_claims_1100_1200_20261017/audits/pr1135_30000052/reviews/package_04/REPORT.md), [review2](https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/blob/f2c69a9d6fc1194aa61bc59459c527eb84615168/draft_pr_actual_claims_1100_1200_20261017/audits/pr1135_30000052/reviews/package_05/REPORT.md). The reviews checked original scope, full mathematics, priority/chronology, new independent controls, all four PDF pages, exact metadata and portable archive reconstruction. [Priority decision and limits](https://github.com/AlecKriebel/Math/blob/f2c69a9d6fc1194aa61bc59459c527eb84615168/draft_pr_actual_claims_1100_1200_20261017/audits/pr1135_30000052/ROOT_PRIORITY_DECISION.md).

**Related work and chronology:** Alper Ferudun's 14 October 2026 [preprint DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23372668](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23372668) explicitly contains the same exact counterexample and broader dimension/exponent results, and is prominently credited throughout the note and metadata. This source PR has GitHub creation record 10 October; the present note is released 17 October. Historical repository public visibility and worldwide first discovery/publication are not certified. No causal inference about awareness, dependence or copying is made. No pre-PR full answer was identified in the bounded current audit; inaccessible full/final bodies and incomplete citation coverage remain documented. A new Fourier proof using classical Su (2000) and Anderson et al. (2007) formulas is correctly labeled a new application, not an older recorded solution. No first-priority claim is made.

AI tools were used extensively in proof development, exact computation, adversarial verification, literature research and writing. The paper and supplements are **unrefereed**; independent AI reviews are not external human peer review or journal acceptance. No individual or other shard was contacted.

Production readback verified the exact reviewed files and metadata. Google Workspace CLI added exactly one DOI row at `'Math Puzzles'!A160:D160` and read it back exactly.
